text:
sophia: Heads-up — Acme Support reported an escalation. Production traffic hitting our function-calling layer is returning downstream 400s. Customer says they see \"schema validation failed\" when the model returns tool args. They attached a repro and logs.

ajay: Thanks. Any immediate P0 impact (broken flows) or noisy errors?

sophia: P0 for them — their support automation is blocked. Volume small (a few reqs/sec) but everything that hits a certain prompt path fails. They included a sample request and the failing tool invocation we got back from the model.

sophia: Repro snippet from their request (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate 
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Create a support ticket: subject=\"Login fails\", priority=high, steps=\"user can't auth\""}],
  "tool_schema": {
    "create_ticket": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"subject": {"type":"string"}, "priority": {"type":"integer"}, "description": {"type":"string"}},
      "required": ["subject","priority"]
    }
  },
  "max_tokens": 200
}
```

sophia: The model returned this tool call (as we received):
```
{
  "tool": "create_ticket",
  "args": {"subject":"Login fails","priority":"high","description":"user can't auth"}
}
```

sophia: Downstream system rejects because priority should be integer (1/2/3). It used \"high\" string. Customer says this used to work with golden prompts earlier.

ajay: Okay, two possible failure modes: model hallucinated wrong type, or our schema translation to the model was ambiguous. Do we have the exact prompt we sent into the model (including schema formatting)?

kyle: I grabbed the request from their logs. We send tool_schema as a JSON schema object (see snippet). The model's output is a plain tool call. Historically we rely on model to follow schema. We should treat this as a regression in tool-calling reliability.

jamal: From runtime logs:
```
[2024-06-22T15:04:10Z] session=abc123 model=redwood-chat-1 -> tool_call parsed: create_ticket args=(subject=\"Login fails\", priority=\"high\", description=\"user can't auth\")
[2024-06-22T15:04:10Z] validator: JSON schema validation failed for create_ticket: /priority: expected integer, got string
```

ajay: Do we have evals for tool-calling that include type checks? I recall we had a schema test harness but maybe it didn't include this prompt family.

eval-ci-bot: CI alert: tool-calling-regression-suite failed on branch release/v2. Test summary: 12 failing, 36 passing. Failing tests include \"ticket-priority-type\" and \"choose-correct-tool-for-escalation\". See: https://ci.redwood.dev/1234

kyle: That's the smoking gun. The regression suite started failing after the model update rolled last night (small kernel/decoding change). We need to triage whether model update changed its propensity to format numeric enums as words.

ajay: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) Add a strict post-parse coercion layer that converts known enum words to ints (e.g., high->3, medium->2, low->1) before validating; 2) Canary rollback of the model update if regression is widespread.

sophia: Customer wants a short-term fix they can rely on. They asked if we can automatically coerce or reject tool calls and return structured error to let them fallback.

kyle: We can implement coercion as a stopgap in the routing layer. But long-term the evals must catch this. We should expand the schema test suite to include golden prompts that cover ordinal enums and numeric vs string variants. Add negative tests where model intentionally returns wrong types.

jamal: I added a reproducer script to the support ticket: run this curl to reproduce locally: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Create a ticket: subject=\"Login fails\", priority=high"}],"tool_schema":{"create_ticket":{"type":"object","properties":{"subject":{"type":"string"},"priority":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["subject","priority"]}},"max_tokens":100}'
```

ajay: Good. Action items:
- ajay: add coercion mapping in router + feature flag (fast)
- kyle: expand tool-calling regression suite with golden prompts & type-variance tests (medium)
- jamal: coordinate with customer and provide an interim webhook that accepts string enums and maps to ints (workaround)
- devops: gate model rollout with the regression suite (prevent automatic deploy)

deploy-bot: Deploy notice: release/v2 model update was rolled out to prod at 2024-06-22T02:12:00Z. Canary 10% -> 100% completed.

kyle: Notes for the regression suite change: create a new test file tests/tool_calling/priority_enum_tests.jsonl with cases for \"1\", 1, \"one\", \"high\", \"urgent\" etc. Each case should assert either coercion mapping or strict rejection depending on runtime policy. Also add a golden prompt file: golden_prompts/priority_enum/golden_001.txt (the exact prompt we saw from Acme).

ajay: Also add a lint rule in the compile pipeline: if tool_schema lists an enum or integer, include an explicit enum mapping in the schema metadata so we can auto-generate coercion rules.

jamal: Customer update: I'll tell Acme we can add router-side coercion within 3 hours behind a feature flag, and follow up with a permanent fix and expanded CI tests. They asked for logs of the failing examples; I've attached a redacted log bundle to the ticket.

sophia: Thanks. Please keep this thread updated. If anyone needs the raw request/response dumps I have them in the support ticket (ticket# 4567).

kyle: I'll start the CI patch now. If eval-ci-bot still flags >5 fails after adding tests we block the model rollout.

eval-ci-bot: New job queued: tool-calling-regression-suite (with added tests) -> job/5678

ajay: TL;DR: root cause likely model regression in formatting enums; mitigation = router-side coercion plus CI expansions to prevent regressions.

sophia: tagging @jamal to keep customer looped, and @kyle for CI work. :thumbsup:
